name: languette
description: A deterministic check against risky actions by coding agents: fail-closed PreToolUse guards for the commands that could ruin a day, such as recursive rm, a disk wipe, a shutdown or a credential pasted into a command.

guard_git_work_loss.title: Guard git work loss
guard_git_work_loss.description: Deny blanket staging (git add -A), stash pop/drop, force pushes, discarding checkouts and git branch -D. Leave on unless you want these git commands through unchecked.

guard_git_work_loss_blanket_staging.title: Block blanket staging
guard_git_work_loss_blanket_staging.description: Deny git add -A, git add . and git commit -a. Leave on unless you want this git command through unchecked. Has no effect while guard_git_work_loss is false.

guard_git_work_loss_stash.title: Block stash pop, drop and clear
guard_git_work_loss_stash.description: Deny git stash pop, clear and a bare drop. Leave on unless you want this git command through unchecked. Has no effect while guard_git_work_loss is false.

guard_git_work_loss_force_push.title: Block force pushes
guard_git_work_loss_force_push.description: Deny bare force pushes, and force pushes or deletes of main or master. Leave on unless you want this git command through unchecked. Has no effect while guard_git_work_loss is false.

guard_git_work_loss_discard.title: Block discarding uncommitted work
guard_git_work_loss_discard.description: Deny git reset --hard, git checkout . or git restore . and git clean -f. Leave on unless you want this git command through unchecked. Has no effect while guard_git_work_loss is false.

guard_git_work_loss_branch_delete.title: Block git branch -D
guard_git_work_loss_branch_delete.description: Deny git branch -D and --delete --force. Leave on unless you want this git command through unchecked. Has no effect while guard_git_work_loss is false.

require_well_formed.title: Deny a command that does not parse
require_well_formed.description: Deny a Bash command the shell parser refuses, with its line and column, before any of it runs. Turned off, the other guards read such a command through a weaker parser instead.

guard_recursive_delete.title: Block recursive rm
guard_recursive_delete.description: Deny recursive rm and find -delete outside scratch areas and generated directories. Leave on unless you want recursive deletes through unchecked.

guard_permissions.title: Block recursive permission changes
guard_permissions.description: Deny recursive chmod, chown and chgrp, chmod 777 and find -exec chmod outside scratch areas. Leave on unless you want permission sweeps through unchecked.

guard_pipe_to_shell.title: Block piping a download into a shell
guard_pipe_to_shell.description: Deny curl, wget or fetch output piped into sh, bash, python and other interpreters, or run through eval or a process substitution. The agent saves the file, reads it, then runs it. Leave on unless you want downloads run unread.

guard_disks.title: Block disk wipes
guard_disks.description: Deny dd onto a device, mkfs, wipefs and shred outside scratch areas, and a redirect or tee onto a disk. Leave on unless you want these through unchecked.

guard_host_availability.title: Block shutdowns and the fork bomb
guard_host_availability.description: Deny shutdown, reboot, halt, poweroff and the fork-bomb shape. Leave on unless you want an agent able to take the machine down.

guard_protected_services.title: Block stopping a protected service
guard_protected_services.description: Deny a systemctl stop, restart or kill of a service named in protected_services. Leave on unless you want an agent able to stop the services your machine depends on.

protected_services.title: Protected services
protected_services.description: Services an agent may not stop, restart or kill with systemctl: unit names, comma-separated, a trailing .service optional, * globs allowed. A name also covers its socket and its @instances. Empty protects none; ssh, the network and the display manager are already guard-host-availability's.

guard_scheduled_jobs.title: Block deleting the crontab
guard_scheduled_jobs.description: Deny crontab -r, which deletes the whole crontab with no undo. Leave on unless you want it through unchecked.

guard_git_stacked_base.title: Block deleting a stacked base branch
guard_git_stacked_base.description: Deny deleting a remote branch that an open pull request is based on or headed from. Leave on unless you want remote branch deletions through unchecked.

guard_duplicate_prs.title: Block a second PR on an issue
guard_duplicate_prs.description: Deny opening a PR that closes an issue an open PR already references, unless the body says it supersedes that PR; ask when GitHub can't say. Leave on unless you want parallel sessions able to open duplicate PRs.

guard_review_threads.title: Block resolving an unanswered bot review thread
guard_review_threads.description: Opt-in, off by default. Deny resolving a review thread a bot commented on unless your reply after the bot's last comment names the fix commit or links the record the dismissal rests on. Turn on if review bots comment on your pull requests and a dismissal should point at a record.

guard_bypass_ruleset.title: Block pushes and merges around a pull-request rule
guard_bypass_ruleset.description: Deny a push to the default branch when GitHub says it requires a pull request, and gh pr merge --admin; ask when GitHub can't say. Leave on unless you want an agent able to use your ruleset bypass.

ask_first.title: Ask before costly commands
ask_first.description: Deny a command the repo lists in .languette/ask-first.json until the user approves that one run through AskUserQuestion. Leave on unless you want those commands through unasked.

guard_bypass_hooks.title: Ask before skipping git hooks
guard_bypass_hooks.description: Deny --no-verify on git commit, push, merge, pull, rebase and am, -n on commit and am, and git -c core.hooksPath= until the user approves that one run through AskUserQuestion. Leave on unless you want agents to skip the repo's hooks unasked.

guard_secrets.title: Keep credentials out of commands
guard_secrets.description: Deny a Bash command holding a known token shape (a GitHub PAT, an AWS key id, a private key header, and more from gitleaks' list), and ask when a value is only named as a credential (DB_PASSWORD=..., --password ..., a URL with a password). The project may add patterns in .languette/secrets.json. Leave on unless you want secrets pasted into commands unchecked.

guard_infra.title: Ask before destroying infrastructure
guard_infra.description: Deny terraform, terragrunt, pulumi, cdk, aws, gcloud, az, kubectl and helm commands that destroy infrastructure or apply without review until the user approves that one run through AskUserQuestion. Plans, previews and dry runs pass. Leave on unless you want those commands through unasked.

guard_github_issues.title: One issue create, transfer or delete per turn
guard_github_issues.description: Deny a second GitHub issue create, transfer or delete in the same human turn, and any inside a loop or xargs. Leave on unless you want issue creates, transfers and deletes through unchecked.

guard_private_terms.title: Keep private terms out of public issues and PRs
guard_private_terms.description: Rewrite your home directory and the pairs in your rewrites file in issue and PR text posted to a public GitHub repo and allow the post, and deny the post if it names a term from your blocked terms file. Leave on unless you want that text through unchecked.

guard_private_terms_anonymize.title: Rewrite home-directory paths to ~ in public posts
guard_private_terms_anonymize.description: Rewrite your home directory, and its other spellings such as /home/<user>, /Users/<user> and /mnt/c/Users/<user>, to ~, and each pair in your rewrites file, in text posted to a public GitHub repo, and allow the post. Needs no file. Leave on unless you want that text posted as written. Has no effect while guard_private_terms is false.

blocked_terms_file.title: Blocked terms file
blocked_terms_file.description: A text file of terms so sensitive that a post naming one is denied whole: one per line, matched case-insensitively as plain text, # for comments. A leading ~ or $HOME is expanded. Unset, ~/.config/languette/blocked-terms.txt is read if it exists; with neither, no term is blocked, and the rewrites still run. A file set here but unreadable, or found but empty, denies every public post.

rewrites_file.title: Rewrites file
rewrites_file.description: A JSON file of pairs rewritten in a post before it leaves: {"rewrite": [["find", "put"], ...]}, matched case-insensitively; a find spelled $NAME is that variable's value, and a pair with no put puts <redacted>. A leading ~ or $HOME is expanded. Unset, ~/.config/languette/rewrites.json is read if it exists; with neither, only the home directory is rewritten. A file set here but unreadable, or found but not in that shape, denies every public post.

private_repos.title: Private repos
private_repos.description: Repos whose issue and PR text is never scanned, as owner/name, comma-separated. Empty by default: every repo is scanned.

guard_signed_comments.title: Experimental, opt-in: sign an agent's GitHub comments as an agent's
guard_signed_comments.description: Experimental and off by default: the signature is one workflow's convention. Deny a PR or issue comment, review or review-thread reply posted through gh, gh api or a GitHub MCP tool unless its body's first line starts with signed_comments_opening and its last line matches signed_comments_signature. If the agent posts under your login, the signature keeps its words from being read as yours. Turn on if your agents sign their comments that way.

signed_comments_opening.title: Signed comments: opening
signed_comments_opening.description: The text a signed comment's first line starts with. Empty means the default, the robot emoji and a space.

signed_comments_signature.title: Signed comments: signature
signed_comments_signature.description: A regular expression a signed comment's last non-empty line must match whole; {session} in it is the first eight hex of the session id. Empty means the default, the robot emoji, model, effort and session. A pattern that does not compile denies every comment.

guard_cross_session_send.title: Check messages to your other sessions
guard_cross_session_send.description: Ask before a session sends a message to another of your sessions, showing the target and the first line; in bypassPermissions, deny the send once the session has read anything from the network. Messages to main and to the session's own subagents and teammates pass. Leave on unless you want sessions to relay untrusted text to each other unseen.

guard_bypass_labels.title: Keep CI-gate bypass labels for humans
guard_bypass_labels.description: Deny a session applying a label named in bypass_labels (none by default) to an issue or PR, through gh, gh api or an MCP tool, in any repo. With bypass_labels empty the guard allows every command.

bypass_labels.title: Bypass labels
bypass_labels.description: Labels a session may not apply: comma-separated, matched case-insensitively. Empty, the default, guards no label: a label that waives a CI gate is the user's to apply unless this names it.

review_thread_logins.title: Review thread reply logins
review_thread_logins.description: Logins, besides the gh login, whose reply lets guard-review-threads pass a resolved review thread: comma-separated, matched case-insensitively, a trailing [bot] ignored. Empty, the default, counts the gh login alone.

prose_budget_commit.title: Check staged prose against the repo's budgets before a commit
prose_budget_commit.description: Warn on a git commit, and let it run, when the prose-budget engine (the prose_budget_command option) finds the staged diff over a repo's own budgets; CI is the gate. A no-op where that engine isn't installed or the repo has no budgets config. Leave on unless you don't want the warning.

prose_budget_command.title: Prose-budget engine
prose_budget_command.description: The command prose_budget_commit runs as its engine, with --staged or --file: an absolute path, a path relative to the session's working directory (before any cd in the command), or a bare name looked up on PATH. Empty means prose-budget on PATH.

guard_worktrees.title: Guard worktrees: no branch switch in $HOME, no reach into another session's worktree
guard_worktrees.description: Opt-in, off by default. Two controls. Deny a git checkout or switch that would change the branch checked out in your home directory, for a $HOME that is itself a work tree (a bare repository over $HOME, or a dotfile manager such as yadm); deny any command or file edit that reaches into a linked git worktree other than the session's own, and EnterWorktree(path=...). Turn on if $HOME is a worktree or you run several sessions against one repo.

guard_worktrees_checkout_home.title: Guard worktrees: control for a branch switch in $HOME
guard_worktrees_checkout_home.description: On by default; applies only when guard_worktrees is on. Set false to keep only the other control.

guard_worktrees_foreign.title: Guard worktrees: control for a reach into another session's worktree
guard_worktrees_foreign.description: On by default; applies only when guard_worktrees is on. Set false to keep only the other control.

record_decisions.title: Record decisions
record_decisions.description: Off by default. Write one line per hook call (each guard's finding, the verdict, the parser rung) to $XDG_STATE_HOME/languette/decisions.jsonl, readable only by you. Nothing leaves the machine; what looks like a secret in the command (a token, a password) is masked.

record_raw_commands.title: Record raw commands
record_raw_commands.description: Off by default; applies only when record_decisions is on. Keep each command and the guards' reasons exactly as written, secrets included.
